tasks.details:

tasks.task: examples/frameworks: Angular interop demo — consume an ignite element (CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA)
tasks.details:
Build a runnable Angular demo under packages/ignite-element/src/examples/frameworks/angular, mirroring the react/vue/svelte scaffolding (vite + source aliases to local ignite-element and the scoped @ignite-element packages; a lightweight Angular + vite setup, no full Angular CLI; pin xstate to the workspace version). Consume the ignite element via Angular standard custom-element path: add CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA to the standalone component (or module) so Angular allows the unknown tag; bind inputs via attribute/property binding; listen to CustomEvents via (eventname) event binding. Document the real Angular friction honestly (CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA requirement, property vs attribute binding semantics, event and zone behavior) and do not paper over it. Do NOT build an igniteAngular helper or directive yet: per-framework wrappers stay follow-ups. Backs the four-frameworks claim (react README) and host-app-integration. Heaviest scaffolding of the three. Acts as an API gap-finder before the breaking cutover. Capture any API gaps as follow-up task briefs BEFORE any source change. Keep minimal and headless-testable; add the new example tsconfig to the packages/ignite-element package.json typecheck chain; extend (do not duplicate) host-app-integration with an Angular section. Precedent: the react/vue/svelte demos. THIRD of the LOCKED sequence Vue then Svelte then Angular then worked-apps; depends on the Svelte demo.
See .fas/tasks/examples-frameworks-angular-interop-demo-consume-an-ignite-e.md

tasks.task: Add named igniteTest rehearsals with trace snapshots
tasks.details:
Add a compact named-rehearsal layer to the existing igniteTest scenario API. Consumers define a rehearsal such as serve-ball with an asserted initial snapshot, one typed object-form command call, and expected final snapshot/view/events, then call await scenario.rehearse("serve-ball") and receive the existing serializable IgniteStorySnapshot trace. Reuse component.record(), story execution, trace serialization, and summary machinery rather than introducing a second recorder or state authority. The initial state is asserted, never injected; consumers provide a fresh isolated runtime when they need repeatable rehearsals, and Ignite must not silently reset shared sources.
See .fas/tasks/add-named-ignitetest-rehearsals-with-trace-snapshots.md

Release: auto-format .changeset/pre.json after 'changeset version' so the Biome format gate stays green. Every beta release, 'changeset version' rewrites .changeset/pre.json in a non-Biome format, tripping the whole-repo Biome format gate (observed for beta.5 and beta.6, each needing a manual 'chore(changeset): format release-generated pre.json' commit). Fix: in scripts/release-beta.mjs, run 'biome format --write .changeset/pre.json' immediately after the 'changeset version' step and before the release commit, so the generated file is committed already formatted. Verify a beta dry-run + real run leaves the format gate clean with no follow-up reformat commit.

Examples: pin the spa-router example's xstate to the workspace version so installing example deps doesn't break the monorepo typecheck. Running 'npm install' in packages/ignite-element/src/examples/spa-router (e.g. to launch the Vite preview) pulls a newer xstate than the workspace pins (observed 5.32.1); 'tsc --project src/examples/spa-router/tsconfig.json' then fails with 'Property getPreInitialState is missing in type StateMachine<...>' — a dual-xstate type skew between the example's machine and ignite's AnyStateMachine. Fix: pin the example's xstate dependency to the exact workspace version (or otherwise ensure the example typecheck resolves xstate from the workspace). Audit the other examples (xstate/redux/mobx) for the same drift and pin them too. Related class: the goodway 'getInitialSnapshot is not a function' spike.

That split is why the examples had to pin to 5.25.0 (the adapter-source copy the example typecheck resolves through); it is fragile and will rot when either side drifts. Keep the peer-dependency range (>=5.19.0) as-is. epics.title: LLM-Authored Projections, Accessibility & Non-Visual Interfaces
epics.goal: Let deterministic Ignite behavior support accessible DOM, text, speech, terminal, and agent-authored interfaces by storing validated projection documents in actor state, exposing authoring commands through igniteTools, and keeping generic inspection, binding, and committer machinery private.
acceptance: The superseded ProjectionRequest/ProjectionSpec registry and command-presentation-metadata design ships no source implementation and remains historical only.

igniteCore keeps its existing source/view/commands/events/effects configuration and custom-element registrar without public registry, bind, inspect, behavior metadata, or adapter-wide projection generics.
Private coherent inspection plus generic projection/binding/committer machinery supports format-specific output without requiring DOM for speech, terminal, or agent paths.

Validated ProjectionDocument data with stable ids, safe semantic nodes, and command-backed actions lives in actor state; raw generated JSX, JavaScript, imports, event handlers, and DOM references are rejected.
LLMs author and incrementally patch projection documents through igniteTools commands, while actor state and command availability remain authoritative.

A voice/text control-center proves prompt or speech input through model tool calls to durable projection state, accessible native JSX, and model-authored speech/text with deterministic CI and optional MLX validation.
Headless tests prove behavior and document contracts; rendered tests separately prove keyboard, focus, accessible names, relationships, and intentional live output.
Final docs teach the minimal public DX, provider/privacy boundaries, actor-web behavior graph alignment, and why voice does not require JSX or DOM.

epics.title: Retained Surfaces and Complex Interface Runtime
epics.goal: Make Ignite Element support canvas, WebGL, editors, maps, video, and high-frequency dashboards through typed callback refs, reserved post-reconciliation commit directives, keyed reconciliation, move-safe resource lifecycle, and evidence-driven scheduling decisions while preserving the existing igniteCore registration API and source authority.
acceptance: The architecture defines a generic retained-surface contract rather than a canvas-specific core API, with source state remaining authoritative and effects remaining consequence-oriented.

Ignite JSX provides typed callback refs and a reserved commit directive with deterministic initial, update, replacement, move, and true-disconnect cleanup semantics without leaking directives to the DOM.
Keyed reconciliation preserves canvas contexts, editor instances, focus, selection, and other retained node state through reorder and fallback paths.
igniteCore gains no commitScheduling surface; retained resources own requestAnimationFrame or microtask cadence until post-dogfood evidence demonstrates a need at the component registration boundary.

A deterministic real-time canvas stress example proves device-pixel-ratio sizing, ResizeObserver handling, consumer-owned requestAnimationFrame interpolation, scoped input, telemetry, and accessible DOM companions.

Downstream validation documents the Actor-Web Mesh Pong adoption contract without moving Actor-Web lifecycle, simulation, transport, or advisory authority into Ignite, and a later evidence task records the no-API verdict or creates a separate scheduler implementation brief.

epics.title: Voice Workbench Statechart Conformance
epics.goal: Make executable statecharts the single lifecycle authority for voice-workbench provider, turn, voice-capture, and speech-delivery workflows while keeping reducers, policies, adapter facts, and Ignite projections in their proper roles.
acceptance: Every lifecycle has an approved machine shape or an explicit reducer, policy/fact, or presentation-only disposition.
The executable session logic prevents responding while the model is preparing or unavailable and exposes fresh isolated actor construction.
Direct xstate/graph tests prove reachability, forbidden combinations, terminal outcomes, recovery, cancellation, timeout, and path coverage.
The model-turn, voice-capture, and speech-delivery workflows have one authoritative owner with typed events, effects, facts, raw snapshots, and derived views.
Any Ignite graph-testing bridge is optional, XState-specific, dogfood-justified, additive to igniteTest, and does not create a second graph engine, recorder, schema, or state authority.
